query_ground_truth.workflow_task: The user was managing unread email triage and urgent alerts, looking up CRM-style trial records, inspecting and modifying source code in GitHub, opening or merging branches, and checking CI workflow failures.
query_ground_truth.intent: Inspect CI workflow run statuses to diagnose and debug failures.

requirement_groups.purpose: check CI workflow run statuses and failures

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if repository identifier may be wrong or access is uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Validate repository access using GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY (avoid 404/permission issues before drilling in).

[Required] [Prerequisite]: List recent automation runs using GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY (paginate with per_page/page; focus on completed runs with failure conclusions, but keep pending runs separate).

[Optional (if you must narrow to a specific workflow)] [Prerequisite]: Enumerate workflows using GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORY_WORKFLOWS (select one, then re-list runs via GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY).
[Optional (if run selection is ambiguous)] [Next Step]: Confirm status/conclusion using GITHUB_GET_A_WORKFLOW_RUN (ensure you’re inspecting the intended run/attempt).
[Required] [Step]: Enumerate jobs for the chosen run using GITHUB_LIST_JOBS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN (include all attempts when reruns exist; identify failed job(s) to target).
[Required] [Step]: Download diagnostic output for each failed job using GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_JOB_LOGS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN (normalize text before searching/parsing).
[Fallback (if per-job logs are missing/truncated)] [Fallback]: Download the full run logs using GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_WORKFLOW_RUN_LOGS (use for complete context across jobs/steps).

[Optional (after applying a fix)] [Next Step]: Re-run only failures using GITHUB_RE_RUN_FAILED_JOBS_FROM_A_WORKFLOW_RUN (then verify by re-fetching with GITHUB_GET_A_WORKFLOW_RUN or re-listing via GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY).
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY] Response payloads can be large and appear truncated in previews; overly tight filters can also yield total_count=0—paginate and broaden criteria to confirm runs exist.
[GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY] Runs may be queued/in_progress where conclusion is null; treat these as pending rather than failed.
[GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY] 404 Not Found commonly indicates a wrong repository identifier or missing access; validate before assuming there are no runs.
[GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_JOB_LOGS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN] Per-job logs can be very large and appear truncated; switch to GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_WORKFLOW_RUN_LOGS when key context is missing.
[GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_JOB_LOGS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN] Log text may include leading encoding artifacts (BOM-like); strip/normalize before searching or parsing.

GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUNS_FOR_A_REPOSITO.description: Lists workflow runs for a repository, allowing filtering by actor, branch, event, status, creation date, check suite ID, or head SHA; the repository must exist and be accessible.

page.description: Page number of the results to fetch.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

actor.description: Filter by the actor's login (e.g., the user who triggered the `push`).

event.description: Filter by the event that triggered the workflow (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`).

owner.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

branch.description: Filter by branch name (e.g., `main` or the branch that triggered the `push`).

status.description: Filter by `status` or `conclusion` (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

created.description: Filter by creation date or date-time range (ISO8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Supports operators like `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `..` for ranges.

head_sha.description: Filter to include only runs associated with the specified `head_sha` (commit SHA at the head of the branch).

exclude_pull_requests.description: Set to `true` to exclude workflow runs triggered by pull request events. Omit or leave as null to include all runs.

GITHUB_LIST_JOBS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_RUN.description: Lists jobs for a specific workflow run in a GitHub repository.

page.description: The page number of the results to fetch. For more details, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the .git extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

owner.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

filter.description: Filters jobs by their `completed_at` timestamp. `latest` returns jobs from the most recent execution attempt of the workflow run. `all` returns all jobs for a workflow run, including from previous execution attempts.

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run for which jobs are to be listed.

per_page.description: The number of results to return per page, with a maximum of 100. For more details, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

GITHUB_DOWNLOAD_JOB_LOGS_FOR_A_WORKFLOW_.description: Downloads logs for a specific job in a GitHub Actions workflow run, contingent on the repository's existence and the job ID being valid and having produced logs.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., user or organization). This name is not case-sensitive.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the job for which to download logs. You can obtain this from the 'List jobs for a workflow run' endpoint.
